content.title: About
content.content: White rice with gravy is cooked polished rice served with a flavorful meat or vegetable sauce. Rice provides a primary source of carbohydrates, while the gravy adds taste and a modest amount of fat.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: White rice is one of the most widely consumed grains worldwide.
There are many types of gravies: tomato, cream, mushroom, meat‑based, etc.
When cooked properly, rice retains a high starch content, making it an excellent energy source.
In several cultures, rice with gravy is featured in special festive dishes.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Rice provides quick‑release glucose, essential for brain function and physical activity.

items.title: Easy to digest
items.content: Cooked white rice is gentle on the stomach and suitable for low‑fiber diets.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: It supplies thiamine, niacin, and vitamin B6, which support metabolism.

items.title: Balanced flavor with gravy
items.content: The gravy contributes a small amount of fat and fat‑soluble vitamins, enhancing nutrient absorption.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: White rice can cause rapid blood‑sugar spikes, which may be problematic for diabetics.

items.title: Sodium in gravy
items.content: Prepared gravies often contain added salt, so monitor sodium intake.

items.title: Low fiber content
items.content: Unlike whole‑grain alternatives, white rice provides little dietary fiber.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve hot as a side dish with meat, fish, or vegetables. Garnish with fresh herbs, a squeeze of lemon, or spices to vary the flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep dry rice in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. Cooked rice with gravy should be cooled quickly and refrigerated, lasting 2‑3 days.
